maria: Heads-up — observed a regression on /stream/generate after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak (commit b3f2). 95th token latency jumps ~90ms starting at token ~160 for some users. Looks like a server-side emit pause rather than network jitter.

infra-bot: deploy completed: prod/k8s: inference-runtime @ b3f2 by @deploy-bot (2026-03-15T04:02Z) :rocket:

sam: Ugh. Saw a few similar traces this morning. Do you have a span showing kernel choice + batch composition? Might be falling back to the scalar kernel for mid-length batches.

maria: Pasted a short snippet from the trace (server-side):

```
[trace] token_index=158 emit_start=2026-03-15T21:03:14.112Z emit_end=2026-03-15T21:03:14.164Z delta=52ms kernel=matmul_v2 batch_len=8 kv_hit_rate=0.18 route=/stream/generate
[trace] token_index=159 emit_start=2026-03-15T21:03:14.164Z emit_end=2026-03-15T21:03:14.170Z delta=6ms kernel=vector_kern batch_len=9 kv_hit_rate=0.20
[trace] token_index=160 emit_start=2026-03-15T21:03:14.170Z emit_end=2026-03-15T21:03:14.262Z delta=92ms kernel=scalar_fallback batch_len=4 kv_hit_rate=0.05
```

maria: Notice how kernel flips around token 160 and the kv_hit_rate drops — possible cache churn or eviction causing small batches that trigger scalar_fallback.

jen: Can we add a quick token-level histogram to Grafana for /stream/generate? Want: token_emit_ms by token_position percentile + kernel label + kv_hit_rate bucketed. That will show correlation with kernel choice.

kai: Repro recipe I used locally: run `wrk -t2 -c50 -d1m` hitting /stream/generate with cached prefixes, then simulate cache eviction with a concurrent job that loads long-prefix requests. Also try toggling the selector flag: `--kernel-selector=legacy` vs `--kernel-selector=heuristic-v2` (the latter is b3f2).

kai: Quick command I run: 
```
# spawn load
./tools/loadgen -c 50 -p 2 -r /stream/generate --prefix-cache-size=200
# simulate churn
./tools/evictor --target=kv --rate=1000
```

sam: If kv_hit_rate falls, batching heuristics shrink batches causing kernel choice to flip. Two hypotheses: (1) the selector's cost model underestimates scalar_fallback penalty for small batch_len on this hw; (2) KV eviction causes extra memory work that pushes emit over the soft_delay SLO and forces smaller batches.

maria: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: increase route soft_delay_ms from 10 -> 25 for /stream/generate to let batches stabilize, and add a canary on 10% traffic with `kernel_selector=legacy`.

jen: I'll add these panels to the perf dashboard and wire an alert: alert when 95th_token_emit_ms > 80ms AND scalar_fallback_rate > 5% over 5m. Panel name: "Token Emit Breakdown (per-route)".

sam: Also add a span tag for `kernel_selected` in client/server traces — right now we only log kernel on server spans. Need both sides to see client ack delta vs server emit pause.

maria: Filed a tiny RFC: https://rwd/infra/rfcs/stream-kernel-observability (link). Plan: 1) add per-token kernel label in traces, 2) expose kernel distribution in route KPIs, 3) run a canary rollback for b3f2 if mitigation doesn't reduce 95th by 30%.

kai: I'll run a profiler on the failing instance set and dump pprof + kernel counters. Expect to see increased memory copy or L2 misses when kv_hit_rate low.

maria: Thanks — can someone pick up the canary change? @sam?

sam: On it, will apply soft_delay bump and start 10% canary with legacy selector in ~15m. Will post results here. :thumbsup:

maria: Great. If we get telemetry before the canary finishes, we can decide to hotfix or rollback.

infra-bot: canary rollout started: prod/k8s inference-runtime canary=10% kernel_selector=legacy (2026-03-15T21:25Z)

sam: Update 21:35Z — early signal: 95th token_emit_ms on canary down from 94ms -> 36ms. Non-canary remains ~88-95ms. Looks promising.

maria: Nice. We'll keep canary running for 30m and then decide. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
